doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Juilliard scholarship as timpanist and his funny timpani story
summary: He studied with a German teacher and had a Juilliard scholarship as a timpanist, sneaking in extra parts until caught.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Uh huh. Where did you learn the harmony required to play the vibes?
Well I studied with a German teacher. I had a scholarship to Juilliard as a timpanist. Want to hear one of my funny stories as a timpanist?

In school, you know, when you hear big symphonies, and the orchestra gets exciting, the timpanist never has a lot to play. Sometimes I had to count a hundred bars and then go ba-ba-ba-boom, ba-boom. A hundred bars and sixty more, boom. Then the orchestra would get exciting and I used to sneak in and make my own parts up. I’d make them up to be exciting with the band. And every fifth day I’d get caught. Every fifth day the band leader would say to me, “Gubenko” he says, “what are you doing?” He says, “Letter C.” I says, “Oh letter C, I was letter D.” He says, “No, you idiot, it was letter C.” So then for five days more I’d play the part like it was written, ba-ba-boom. And then I’d start sneaking. Because I always thought there should be more timpanis when the orchestra got exciting — that bottom with the timpani you know. But that’s how they’re writing. Five days for him, five days for me.
That’s great. So you got some classical —quote — training.
